root_idea.summary: The root expresses remoteness as the opposite of nearness, and succession as the counterpart of what comes before.
root_idea.development: Its meanings extend from physical distance to conceptual remoteness, separation and estrangement, temporal succession, alienation, and—in particular constructions—perishing or imprecation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I verb; the evidence includes both بَعُدَتْ and the variant بَعِدَتْ.
Displayed under the normalized perfect-tense citation form.
Displayed under the adjective citation form بَعِيد.
Displayed as the nominal/adverbial noun بَعْد.
Displayed as the verbal noun بُعْد.
Displayed under the normalized singular passive-participle citation form مُبْعَد; the Quran occurrence is plural.
The T-tagged group is the same lexical item بَعْد used adverbially and is merged with the noun/adverbial-noun public form.

senses.definition: to become distant, remote, or far away
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic group contains the surface forms بَعُدَتْ and بَعِدَتْ; the sense denotes becoming distant or removed.
A distinct Quranic use, especially associated with the بَعِدَ form and the expression concerning Thamud; the lexical sources also report disagreement about using بَعُدَ in this sense.

senses.definition: to make distant, put far apart, or widen the separation between
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively for extending the distance or separation between persons, places, or journeys; the Quranic construction is an imperative request to make the spaces between journeys far apart.

senses.definition: far, distant, remote, or extended in spatial or temporal distance
senses.usage_conditions: Used of physical distance and, by extension, of an extended interval, range, or remoteness from something.

senses.definition: far removed in an abstract or evaluative sense; far astray, remote from truth, or far-fetched
senses.usage_conditions: May describe conceptual or moral remoteness, including a state from which return to guidance is difficult, or a saying far from what is correct.
A temporal noun or adverb, often governing a following genitive complement or occurring with an understood complement, including after a person, event, statement, or action.

senses.definition: after that in the sense of despite or notwithstanding that
senses.usage_conditions: A reported Quranic construction in which بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ is interpreted as meaning مع ذلك, “notwithstanding that.”

senses.definition: before, in a reported contrary interpretation of after
senses.usage_conditions: A disputed interpretation reported for Quranic expressions in 79:30 and 21:105; it is not the ordinary temporal sense and is attributed to a minority reading or explanation.
The noun denotes distance itself, whether literal or relational; in Quranic usage it may occur as an expression of separation or distance.

senses.definition: away with; an imprecation of removal, alienation, or perdition
senses.usage_conditions: Used in an imprecatory formula wishing a people removal from good or prosperity, and by extension expressing their perdition or destruction.

senses.definition: removed far away; kept at a distance
senses.usage_conditions: Passive result of causing someone or something to be distant, remote, or removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to be far from probability or correctness; to be improbable, extraordinary, or strange
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a saying, event, or matter judged remote from what is probable or correct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to exceed the proper bounds in bargaining or in demanding a price
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use in offering or negotiating a sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression أَخَذَهُ مَا قَرُبَ وَمَا بَعُدَ: to be overtaken by both recent and old griefs
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic construction contrasting what is near or recent with what is distant or old.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to become far removed from one's home or native country; to become a stranger or estranged there
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical branch distinct from merely being physically distant and from the Quranic perishing use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to declare someone or something far removed, especially from evil
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II construction; the supplied entry also cross-references the broader causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to become distant from another or to be in a different part, quarter, or tract
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III use describing separation or occupying a different region, rather than the Quranic causative command to widen distances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to make or cause distant; to remove, send away, alienate, or estrange
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV branch, including imprecatory language wishing someone alienation from good or prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: How far it is from what is right or correct!
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an exclamatory construction about a saying or judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: to become mutually distant, remote, or estranged; to withdraw from one another
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VI reciprocal or reflexive branch, including estrangement from family or friends and mutual withdrawal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: behind in place; beyond; with nothing further or no higher degree beyond it
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A less common spatial or limiting use of the adverbial noun, distinct from its ordinary temporal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: now then; a formula marking transition in an address or discourse
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression used after introductory praise, prayer, or preliminary remarks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a little after; shortly after
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The diminutive form denotes a time near to the preceding event or time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: yet or as yet
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially common in negative expressions such as “he has not died yet.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: remoteness from probability or correctness; improbability or strangeness
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun use describing a matter as extraordinary or unlikely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: penetrating, profound, or far-reaching judgment and prudence
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing a person as possessing depth or effectiveness of judgment; it may also describe going far in hostility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: far-reaching in purpose, ambition, or design; long-standing in time or acquaintance; extraordinary in its kind
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical extensions concerning an intention, a long interval, or an unusual affair, not treated as separate Quranic senses here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: distant in kinship or relationship; a stranger or remote dependent
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In this relational sense the adjective may describe persons who are not close relations or immediate companions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: perishing, or far removed from one's home and native country in estrangement
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate unclassified lexical headword, not simply an inflectional form of the Quranic بَعِيد entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: more distant, most distant, or farther removed, including in relationship
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparative and superlative form may describe spatial distance, remote sources, or a more distant relation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: more or most extreme, excessive, egregious, or extraordinary in its kind
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an unusual degree or of a person lacking excellence, power, or anything of value.

other_classical_meanings.definition: the remote one, especially one remote from good, continence, intelligence, or faithfulness
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A euphemistic or indirect epithet in malediction and dispraise; the evidence reports senses including foolishness and treachery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: a man who makes far journeys
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use for a person characterized by undertaking distant travel.

cautions: The Form I Quran group contains both بَعُدَتْ and بَعِدَتْ; the perishing sense is especially associated with the latter and is subject to classical disagreement about the two vocalisms.
The interpretation of بَعْدَ as “before” in the cited Quran passages is explicitly disputed and should not be treated as its ordinary meaning.
The public مُبْعَد citation is normalized to the singular passive participle although the supplied Quran occurrence is plural.
